opportunities.title: No published LLM benchmark results
opportunities.detail: Neither of the two multilingual benchmarks we track reports this language. Adding it would give builders and buyers a baseline.
opportunities.why: About 5.5 million Quechua speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.4 million within five years. Ready to use: FLORES-200 (covers this language); FineWeb-2 (9 million words).

opportunities.title: No published speech recognition error rate
opportunities.detail: The language isn't in the published FLEURS error-rate breakdowns we track, so builders can't tell how usable open speech recognition is.
opportunities.why: About 6.9 million Quechua speakers are online today, and that should reach 8.1 million within five years. Ready to use: YODAS2 (1.7 hours of transcribed speech); Mozilla Common Voice (178 hours of transcribed speech).

opportunities.title: No major speech input service, though open resources exist
opportunities.detail: Open datasets hold 180 hours of transcribed speech, and an open model lists the language.
opportunities.why: About 6.9 million Quechua speakers are online today, and that should reach 8.1 million within five years. Ready to use: YODAS2 (1.7 hours of transcribed speech); Mozilla Common Voice (178 hours of transcribed speech).

opportunities.title: No cloud text-to-speech voice found, though open resources exist
opportunities.detail: None of the cloud services checked has a voice for this language. An open text-to-speech model already speaks it. Open datasets hold 180 hours of transcribed speech.
opportunities.why: About 6.9 million Quechua speakers are online today, and that should reach 8.1 million within five years. Ready to use: MMS text-to-speech (covers this language); YODAS2 (1.7 hours of transcribed speech).

opportunities.title: An open text recognition model exists, but no major service
opportunities.detail: An open OCR model reads printed text in this language. Text recognition also turns printed books into training data for every other technology.
opportunities.why: About 5.5 million Quechua speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.4 million within five years. Ready to use: Tesseract OCR (covers this language); FineWeb-2 (9 million words).

opportunities.title: No reading-comprehension benchmark
opportunities.detail: Belebele, the widest multilingual reading benchmark, doesn't include this language yet.
opportunities.why: About 5.5 million Quechua speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.4 million within five years. Ready to use: FLORES-200 (covers this language).

opportunities.title: Translation is offered by 2 of 3 major services
opportunities.detail: An open model and the FLORES-200 evaluation set already cover this language, so the main remaining step is a product launch.
opportunities.why: About 5.5 million Quechua speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.4 million within five years. Ready to use: NLLB-200 (covers this language); FLORES-200 (covers this language).

opportunities.title: The interface is translated on 2 of 3 major platforms
opportunities.detail: People can already use some phone and computer platforms in this language. Shared terminology would make the remaining ones faster to translate.
opportunities.why: About 5.5 million Quechua speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.4 million within five years. Ready to use: Unicode CLDR (modern coverage).

opportunities.title: A keyboard layout exists but isn't on every major platform
opportunities.detail: A layout ships on 2 of 3 major keyboards. Contributing it to CLDR Keyboards, the open interchange format for layouts, would let any platform adopt it.
opportunities.why: About 5.5 million Quechua speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.4 million within five years. Ready to use: Keyman keyboards (covers this language); Unicode CLDR (modern coverage).

opportunities.title: Wikipedia has 64 active editors
opportunities.detail: A small editing community limits new open text. Edit-a-thons and translation drives with universities have grown communities elsewhere.
opportunities.why: About 5.5 million Quechua speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.4 million within five years.

opportunities.title: Only about 9 million words of open web text
opportunities.detail: Little text online limits language models and word prediction. Digitising books and news archives is often the fastest route.
opportunities.why: About 5.5 million Quechua speakers are online and able to text today, and that should reach 6.4 million within five years.
